description: The chart presents the distribution of problem difficulty levels categorized by correctness under two settings: with knowledge (w/ knowledge) and without knowledge (w/o knowledge), using Chain of Thought (CoT) and another method. It is divided into three pie charts, each representing a different difficulty level: easy, medium, and hard. The easy level has four slices, with the largest slice representing 45.9% of problems solved with knowledge, followed by 40.6% without knowledge, 10.1% with knowledge and knowledge reasoning, and 3.3% without knowledge and knowledge reasoning. The medium level also has four slices, with the largest slice representing 44.3% of problems solved with knowledge, followed by 44.6% without knowledge, 7.2% with knowledge and knowledge reasoning, and 3.9% without knowledge and knowledge reasoning. The hard level has four slices as well, with the largest slice representing 36.8% of problems solved with knowledge, followed by 36.2% without knowledge, 20.1% with knowledge and knowledge reasoning, and 7.0% without knowledge and knowledge reasoning. The slices are color-coded to represent the different categories, and the percentages are labeled within each slice. The chart does not include a legend, but the color coding is consistent across the three pie charts.
